title: Risk of Bone Fracture due to Spaceflight-induced Changes to Bone
organization: NASA Human Research Program / NASA Johnson Space Center (NTRS record)
license_basis: NASA Technical Reports Server record of a NASA Human Research Program evidence report authored by NASA civil servants and NASA contractors (KBR). Treated as a US government work; only the NTRS abstract text was quoted. Contractor authorship means public-domain status is likely but not certain.
key_findings: HRP assesses later fracture risk in active astronauts with a biomechanical approach; active and retired astronauts are tested triennially for premature primary osteoporosis.
Analysis of fractures in health records of the full astronaut cohort suggests a higher incidence of hip and spine fractures after longer-duration flights than after shorter ones.

Routine pre-to-postflight DXA does not fully detect bone loss and recovery in long-duration astronauts, nor full recovery of hip trabecular bone; hip QCT delineates effects of spaceflight, countermeasures and recovery on cortical and trabecular bone.
QCT distinguishes the effects of alendronate and of ARED resistive exercise on specific bone sub-regions during spaceflight.
Accelerated hip trabecular vBMD loss during spaceflight may be analogous to menopause-related accelerated loss in females.
The IMPACT probabilistic risk assessment tool is in development and was not included in the 2024 update.
limitations: Only the NTRS metadata and abstract were read; the full evidence report PDF was not read.
The abstract refers both to an 'updated 2023 Fracture Evidence Report' and to 'this 2024 update' (as written in the source).
Several abstract bullet points contain garbled bullet characters in the NTRS API text, so they were paraphrased rather than quoted.
